title: Chicken Velouté
description: A pale, silky mother sauce made from chicken stock and a blond roux. The base for sauce suprême and a chicken version of allemande.
ingredients: 600 mL unsalted white chicken stock, plus extra as needed
Salt and ground white pepper, to taste
steps: Melt the butter in a heavy saucepan over medium-low heat. Stir in the flour and cook 2–3 minutes, stirring, until pale blond with no raw flour aroma. Do not brown it.
Remove briefly from the heat and gradually whisk in the stock, starting with small additions to make a smooth paste.
Bring to a gentle simmer while stirring, then cook on low for 25–30 minutes. Stir frequently along the bottom and skim any skin or foam.
Aim for about 500 mL and a light coating consistency. Thin with stock if necessary, or simmer a little longer to thicken. Strain for an especially smooth finish.
Season lightly if using as a base for another sauce; season to taste if serving directly.
notes: White chicken stock is made without roasting the bones and keeps the sauce pale. A stock rich in gelatin gives better body. Serve with chicken, pork tenderloin, vegetables, or rice. Use this recipe as the base for Sauce Suprême or Sauce Allemande. For a traditional veal velouté, substitute unsalted white veal stock.
